question: ap1
constraint: without any genetic perturbation (no knockouts, knockdowns, CRISPR, or overexpression)
prompt:
Constraint: every one of your ideas must be carried out without any genetic perturbation (no knockouts, knockdowns, CRISPR, or overexpression). Within that constraint, make the ideas as informative as possible.

Research question: "What analyses or measurements would best test whether AP-1 acts as a cellular memory mechanism?"

Propose 5 distinct, concrete ideas (analyses, measurements, or experiments) that a research lab could pursue to address this question. For each idea give a short title and a description of one or two sentences.

ideas.title: Priming-and-rechallenge time course with chromatin accessibility readout
ideas.description: Expose cells (e.g., fibroblasts, macrophages, or keratinocytes) to a transient AP-1-activating stimulus such as TPA, EGF, or wounding cues, wash it out, and rechallenge after days to weeks. Compare transcription and ATAC-seq/CUT&Tag (H3K27ac, H3K4me1) in primed versus naive cells to ask whether response magnitude and kinetics persist after AP-1 activity itself has returned to baseline.

ideas.title: Longitudinal single-cell multiome tracking of AP-1 motif accessibility and gene expression
ideas.description: Run paired scRNA/scATAC-seq (or lineage-barcoded sampling) at multiple times before, during, and long after transient stimulation, and quantify whether FOS/JUN family motif-accessible regions (e.g., ChromVAR scores) stay open in the subset of cells that previously had high AP-1 activity. Linking prior AP-1 dose to later accessibility and responsiveness at single-cell level distinguishes true heritable memory from population heterogeneity.

ideas.title: Live-cell reporter imaging of AP-1 dynamics and inheritance across divisions
ideas.description: Use cells carrying a knock-in-free, transient or lentiviral-free approach is not needed: instead, apply a non-integrating AP-1 transcriptional reporter or live-cell dyes/antibody-fragment imaging in endogenous cells and track single-cell AP-1 activity through repeated stimulations and cell divisions with lineage reconstruction. Correlating mother and daughter responses and past history with present response tests whether memory is cell-autonomous and mitotically heritable, and whether it depends on pulse frequency or duration.

ideas.title: Pharmacological dissection of maintenance mechanisms
ideas.description: After priming, apply small-molecule inhibitors at distinct windows, such as JNK/MAPK inhibitors, BAF/SWI-SNF ATPase inhibitors, HDAC/HAT (p300/CBP) inhibitors, or DNA/histone methylation inhibitors, either during priming or only during the memory interval, and then rechallenge. Whether memory is lost when each is applied during establishment versus maintenance reveals if AP-1 binding, continuous signaling, or chromatin changes carry the memory.

ideas.title: Genomic footprinting and pioneer-activity profiling in natural in vivo injury/inflammation models
ideas.description: Profile cells from tissues after resolved natural perturbations (e.g., skin wounding, inflammation, or aged vs. young tissue) using ATAC-seq, CUT&RUN for JUN/FOS, and Hi-C or HiChIP, and compare with matched naive tissue. Persistent AP-1 motif footprints, retained enhancer-promoter loops, and faster re-induction of target genes on a second injury, correlated with the motif-containing regions that were opened by the first event, would support AP-1-dependent memory under physiological conditions without genetic manipulation.
